h: The Three Crowns and the Holiness of the Royal Table

p: the bas that is crowned with the Avos."
בַּלַּיְלָה נֶגֶד יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
at night, corresponding to Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him;
וּבַבּוֹקֶר כְּנֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
in the morning, corresponding to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him;
corresponding to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him.
And in the Minchah prayer of Shabbos,
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן כְּנֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which likewise corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him
there is a change in the wording of the prayers on Shabbos,
like the change in the sanctities of the meals,
which is not so on Yom Tov,
where the sanctities of the meals are one,
and so too the wording of the prayers,
in this prayer all the Avos are mentioned.
The reason is that Yaakov Avinu
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב קעה, ב)
(as is written in the holy Zohar II 175b),
for he includes also the holiness of Avraham and Yitzchak;
were included in the holiness of Yaakov as well,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תּוֹלְדוֹת)
(as they said in Bereishis Rabbah 63:3, at the beginning of Toldos).
That is, the name Yisrael indicates
אָז נִתְבָּרֵר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
it then became clear regarding Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
כִּי בְיִצְחָק יִקָּרֵא לְךָ זָרַע (בְּרֵאשִׁית כא, יב)
that "through Yitzchak shall offspring be called yours" (Bereishis 21:12),
and Yishmael is not included in the offspring of Avraham;
and regarding Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him, it became clear:
"through Yitzchak, but not all of Yitzchak,"
אַךְ זֶהוּ רַק אַחַר שֶׁנּוֹלַד יַעֲקֹב
But this was only after Yaakov was born,
וְנִקְרְאוּ אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק גַּם כֵּן אָז יִשְׂרָאֵל
and then Avraham and Yitzchak too were called Yisrael.
there was dross in their offspring:
Yishmael was included in the offspring of Avraham,
"If only Yishmael might live before You!"
and Esav was included in the offspring of Yitzchak.
and the attribute of "bas" is crowned with them.
that of the Altar, Aharon merited it and took it;
that of the Table, David merited it and took it;
that of the Aron still lies waiting, etc."
These correspond to the crown of kehunah,
the crown of kingship, and the crown of Torah,
as is written in Rashi's commentary.
who correspond to the three pillars:
Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
who corresponds to the pillar of gemilus chassadim:
his occupation was with the attribute of love,
from which comes alacrity in the positive mitzvos,
as they said in the Yerushalmi (Berachos 9:5, perek HaRo'eh);
and we find in the Gemara (Chullin 16a):
קְרָא זְרִיזוּתֵיהּ דְּאַבְרָהָם קָא מַשְׁמַע לָן
"The verse is teaching us the alacrity of Avraham."
And he corresponds to the crown of kingship,
for the occupation of the king
is to see to the needs of his people,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ אֵצֶל דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
as we find with David HaMelech, peace be upon him:
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אֶצְלוֹ (בְּרֵאשִׁית יד, יז)
And so we find it said regarding Avraham (Bereishis 14:17):
אֶל עֵמֶק שָׁוֵה הוּא עֵמֶק הַמֶּלֶךְ
"to the Valley of Shaveh, which is the King's Valley";
that there all the nations came to one accord, etc.:
And Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
corresponds to the pillar of avodah,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה בָּא הַזְּהִירוּת בְּמִצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
from which comes carefulness in the negative mitzvos,
as they said in the Yerushalmi.
"Here, I offered up my soul before You,"
He corresponds to the pillar of avodah,
which is the crown of kehunah,
And Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
corresponds to the crown of Torah.
Yet each one of the Avos
has all three crowns included in him.
that it is said of him (Tehillim 110:4):
וּבוֹ הִתְחִיל הַשְּׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ט, א)
and with him began the two thousand years of Torah (Avodah Zarah 9a).
"The Torah comes from the side of Gevurah"
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג פ, סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)
וְכֶתֶר מַלְכוּת מָצִינוּ בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן
and the crown of kingship we find in him as well,
to make a covenant with him,
and it is not the way of kings
to make a covenant except with a king.
rather than the silver and gold of Avimelech";
and this is the crown of kingship,
which is the table of kings,
that kings do not come to poverty,
and as is written in Rashi's commentary:
"for his treasury stands as it stood."

p: for the Rabbis are called kings,
וּבְנֵי דָוִד כֹּהֲנִים הָיוּ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב ח, יח)
"And the sons of David were Kohanim" (Shmuel II 8:18):
just as a Kohen takes first,
so too a talmid chacham takes first.
וְזֶה הַמָּקוֹר לְדִבְרֵי הָרַמְבַּ״ם זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
And this is the source for the words of the Rambam, of blessed memory
"And not the tribe of Levi alone,
and who has cast off from his neck the yoke
such a person has become sanctified as holy of holies,
and Hashem will be his portion and his inheritance, etc."
Now, the crown of the Altar:
Aharon merited it and took it,
for himself and for his descendants after him;
and likewise the crown of kingship:
David merited it and took it;
but that of the Aron lies waiting,
for Moshe Rabbeinu did not bequeath
his greatness to his descendants after him.
And at the time of Matan Torah,
they tied to each and every one of Yisrael
corresponds to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
whose occupation was with the attribute of love
and alacrity in the positive mitzvos,
whose attribute was dread and fear
and carefulness in the negative mitzvos.
that one hears with this ear and lets it out with that one,
but that it should enter the heart,
so that he will not transgress it;
"The ear that heard at Har Sinai,
'For the Children of Yisrael are servants to Me'
and he went and acquired a master for himself,
In the same vein Rashi explained from the Mechilta
"The ear that heard at Har Sinai
At first glance, what is the ear guilty of, that it should be pierced?
let the organs of action be pierced,
But it is as we said:
it would have entered the heart,
and he would not have transgressed what he heard;
as the fumigating frame is to garments, etc.;
the two hundred forty-eight limbs of a person
And this is the crown of "nishma":
that it be fixed in the heart,
to guard oneself from violating a negative commandment;
that were on the vessels of the Mikdash,
that of the Altar being a sign for the crown of kehunah
and that of the Aron a sign for the crown of Torah
אַךְ שֶׁל שֻׁלְחָן סִימָן לְכֶתֶר מַלְכוּת
But that of the Table being a sign for the crown of kingship,
because the Table is a sign for the wealth of kings;
was the one that stood before Hashem,
וְאֵיזוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת יֵשׁ לוֹ לְשֻׁלְחַן מְלָכִים
so what connection does it have to the table of kings?
and not the delicacies of kings.
in line with what we have said
and do not crave the table of kings,
for your table is greater than their table."
how does it make sense to say
to someone accustomed to bread with salt,
water by measure, and a life of hardship,
that he might crave the table of kings?
It is enough for him to crave
"for your table is greater than their table":
if it refers to Olam Haba,
וְשֻׁלְחַן מְלָכִים הוּא רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
while the table of kings is only in Olam Hazeh,
they are not of one kind,
and the term "greater" does not apply,
as the Rambam wrote (in the Shemonah Perakim).
Rather, the meaning of "the table of kings"
is that the eating should be in holiness,
from which words of Torah were made,
and it was written in the Nevi'im for all eternity.
And perhaps one will feel envious:
לָמָּה הוּא לֹא יוּכַל לִזְכּוֹת לָזֶה
why can he not merit this,
in the feast of Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him?
וְלָמָּה הוּא מוּכְרָח לְהִצְטַעֵר בְּפַת בַּמֶּלַח
Why must he suffer with bread and salt,
as is the way of Torah,
that his eating be in holiness,
which is the table of kings?
"And do not crave the table of kings,
for your table is greater than their table."
This is in line with what is written
is the sustenance of the companions,
those who toil in Torah, etc.;
'Wisdom gives life to those who possess it.'"
Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him,
who was a chariot for the attribute of Malchus,
which is the Torah she'b'al peh,
in a dream, from the side of Hashem Yisbarach;
through their own effort and toil,
which is "wisdom gives life to those who possess it,"
וְעַל זֶה הָיָה מוֹרֶה הַזֵּיר שֶׁעַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן
This is what the crown on the Table signified
דְּאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קנד, ב)
for it is stated in the holy Zohar (II 154b)
so that all their eating would be in holiness
וְלֹא יִהְיֶה מֵהֶן קִטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרָע
and no accusation of the yetzer hara would arise from it;
and this is "the table of kings."
And David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
although he was a chariot for the attribute of Malchus,
that his eating would be in holiness,
and this is a further restriction,
as they said in the Yerushalmi (Pe'ah 4:2)
עַל הַפָּסוּק (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כב, יד)
"And I, in my affliction, have prepared,"
and consecrate his meal to Heaven.
And Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him,
of whom it is written (Divrei HaYamim I 29:23):
"And he sat upon the throne of Hashem,"
and who merited all of the lower wisdom,
the aspect of "Malchus is the mouth,"
which we call Torah she'b'al peh,
he merited the table of kings,
for his feast was written in the Torah for all eternity.
And this is the meaning of what they said in the Gemara
a feast like that of Shlomo in his time,
you have not fulfilled your obligation to them,
for they are the children of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov."
and Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov are called kings;
שֶׁהֲרֵי הָרְאָיָה הִיא רַק מִסְּעוּדַת אַבְרָהָם
for the proof there comes only from the feast of Avraham,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הִזְכִּיר יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב גַּם כֵּן
and nevertheless it mentioned Yitzchak and Yaakov as well.
we find that kingship pertains to him,
as it says, "to the King's Valley,"
to make a covenant with him,
But Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
וְהָיָה מַכְנִיעַ אֶת עַצְמוֹ נֶגֶד עֵשָׂו
and he humbled himself before Esav;
so in what sense is he called a king?
But it is as we said:
what is meant by "the table of kings"
is that one's eating be in holiness;
וְזֶה הָיָה חֵלֶק יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and this was the portion of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
meaning that Hashem Yisbarach is the shepherd
and evil does not go forth from Him,
and such eating comes only from the good.
"and He will give me bread to eat,"
meaning that Hashem Yisbarach would be the One Who feeds
and the eating would be in holiness.
And regarding Shabbos, it is stated in Pri Etz Chaim
that Moshe Rabbeinu returns the crowns to Yisrael,
the crown of "naaseh" and the crown of "nishma,"
which correspond to Avraham and Yitzchak.
And all agree that the Torah was given on Shabbos
and especially at the third meal,
and we merit the crown of Torah,
includes all three crowns, as stated.
Therefore we mention all three Avos,
who correspond to the three crowns,
